title: Committee of Supply – Head M (Ministry of Finance)
what_it_is: Committee of Supply – Head M (Ministry of Finance)

sections.label: Rising operating and development expenditures
sections.summary: The Paper shows operating and development expenditures rising, possibly sharply, towards recurring spending of about 20% of GDP by 2030, driven by healthcare, wage subsidies, security and social spending.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: It is clear from the Paper that both our operating and development expenditures are rising, and may rise sharply in the years ahead.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: We look set to be heading towards a recurring spending bill of about 20% of our GDP by 2030.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: The key drivers are expected: healthcare, wage subsidies, security and other social spending.

sections.label: NIRC and expansionary Budget
sections.summary: The Net Investment Returns Contribution, currently 20% of revenue, means the Budget will always be expansionary because expenditures exceed taxes collected.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: The fact that we have a significant Net Investment Returns Contribution (NIRC) contribution to our Budget every year, currently at 20% of our revenue, would mean that our Budget would necessarily be expansionary.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: Our expenditures are way higher than the taxes that we collect from the system.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: Hence, from that angle, our Budget will always be expansionary if we rely on NIRC to balance our books.

sections.label: Sports Hub payment and COVID-19 report
sections.summary: It asks whether the Sports Hub termination payment was so urgent it had to be advanced from the Contingencies Fund rather than Budget 2023, and when the $72 billion COVID-19 expenditure financial report will be completed.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Was the termination payment for the Sports Hub so urgent, that it had to be advanced from the Contingencies Fund and not paid out of the Budget 2023?

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Fourth, when will the financial report on the $72 billion COVID-19 expenditure be completed?

sections.label: President's approval of fiscal amendments
sections.summary: Minister Indranee Rajah said unsupported amendments would not be put to the President, suggesting the President's power to approve fiscally significant legislation follows Cabinet's advice.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: In the exchange, I was told the Presidential approval had not been obtained on my proposed amendments.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: I asked the Government when these amendments had been referred to the President to obtain the decision to which Minister Indranee Rajah made this reply and I am quoting a little from the longest speech she made in the interest of time, "We determine that my amendments could not be supported, the reasons explained earlier by my colleagues and, as the amendments could not be supported, they will not put forward to the President for the President's recommendation." From this, it would seem that the exercise of the President's power to approve legislation that has fiscal implications has to be according to the Cabinet's advice.

sections.label: Cabinet deeming President's decision
sections.summary: It notes the matter was not referred to the President and asks the rationale for constitutional provisions letting the Cabinet deem the President to have said yes or no.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: And it did say that that particular matter had not been referred to the President.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: And secondly, and much more importantly, what is the rationale for having such provisions in the Constitution whereby the Cabinet can deem the President to have said "yes" or "no" on certain matters and, hence, decide by itself?

sections.label: Reserves and COVID-19 pandemic
sections.summary: Success in weathering the COVID-19 pandemic came largely from using deep financial reserves accumulated by a Government that spent public monies responsibly and prudently.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Mr Chairman, our success in weathering the recent COVID-19 pandemic came down largely to our ability to utilise our deep financial reserves, which have been accumulated by the Government who has spent public monies responsibly and prudently.

sections.label: SMEs in Singapore economy
sections.summary: SMEs make up 99% of businesses in Singapore, employ nearly seven in 10 workers and contribute close to half of GDP.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Mr Chairman, Sir, SMEs make up 99% of all businesses in Singapore's economy, employing nearly seven out of 10 workers and contributing close to half of our GDP.

sections.label: Procurement opportunities open to SMEs
sections.summary: In 2021, more than 80% of procurement opportunities were open to SMEs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: In 2021, more than 80% of the procurement opportunities were open to SMEs.

sections.label: Tender-lite system for SMEs
sections.summary: An in-between middle ground can exist where a tender-lite system provides SMEs and startups procurement opportunities more readily.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: An “in-between” or middle ground can exist, where there is a “tender-lite system” which can provide SMEs and startups procure opportunities more readily.

sections.label: US energy security climate investment
sections.summary: The US invests $391 billion in energy security and climate provisions, including tax incentives and a green bank, with $3 per kg hydrogen tax credits.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Investing $391 billion in provisions related to energy security and climate change, including tax incentives and a green bank.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: The tax credits of $3 per kg of hydrogen is particularly notable, turning the US into one of the cheapest countries in the world to produce green hydrogen.

sections.label: Philanthropy Tax Incentive Scheme
sections.summary: The Philanthropy Tax Incentive Scheme for Family Offices announced in Budget 2023 facilitates philanthropy and supports Singapore's ambition to be Asia's philanthropic hub.

sentences.speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
sentences.text: The Philanthropy Tax Incentive Scheme announced in Budget 2023 for Family Offices is another important step to facilitate philanthropy and to meet Singapore’s ambition to be Asia's philanthropic hub.

sections.label: Philanthropists supporting climate solutions
sections.summary: A McKinsey climate philanthropy report notes philanthropists possess resources and expertise to support climate mitigation and adaptation solutions, especially where market support may lack.

sentences.speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
sentences.text: As a recent McKinsey climate philanthropy report has noted, philanthropists possess both resources and expertise to support climate mitigation and adaptation solutions, especially in areas that may lack market support.

sections.label: Government expenditure and GDP
sections.summary: Singapore's overall performance has been good, with current Government expenditure around 18% of GDP.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: Singapore’s overall performance has been good, with current Government expenditure being around 18% of GDP.

sections.label: Cost avoidance in 2022
sections.summary: In 2022, total cost avoidance of around $1 billion was achieved through this process.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: In 2022, we achieved total cost avoidance of around $1 billion through this process.

sections.label: VITAL demand aggregation savings
sections.summary: VITAL's Demand Aggregation contracts for common buys saved the Government more than $50 million per annum.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: Another example is VITAL’s Demand Aggregation contracts for common buys such as office supplies, catering and courier services.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: These saved the Government more than $50 million per annum.

sections.label: SMEs and Tender Lite
sections.summary: About 80% of Government contracts go to SMEs annually, and MOF will introduce Tender Lite by end-2023.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: SMEs participate actively in our Government contracts and about 80% of these are awarded to SMEs annually.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: To further improve the access of SMEs to business opportunities through Government tenders, MOF will introduce a new category of tender by the end of 2023 called “Tender Lite”, which comes with fewer and simpler conditions.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: Tender Lite will allow more suppliers to participate in tenders with value higher than $90,000 but below $1 million and is estimated to cover over 70% of all Government tenders that are currently awarded to SMEs.

sections.label: Sustainability in Government procurement
sections.summary: Environmental sustainability requirements and evaluation criteria will be included in all Government procurement within five years, starting FY2024 for large construction and ICT tenders.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: Our target is to include environmental sustainability requirements and evaluation criteria into all Government procurement within the next five years, in a manner that keeps pace with industry readiness and international developments.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: Starting from FY2024, for tenders of construction projects and ICT projects with minimum estimated procurement value of $50 million and $10 million respectively, we will set aside up to 5% of the evaluation points for sustainability-related considerations.

sections.label: Strengthening social compact and economy
sections.summary: These efforts will strengthen the social compact and build a more caring and inclusive Singapore, supporting pro-growth policies and economic growth together.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: Through such efforts, we will strengthen our social compact and build a more caring and inclusive Singapore.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: This will then provide the social cohesion and stability for us to pursue pro-growth policies and enlarge our economic pie, generate more opportunities and provide more resources that we can then use to invest in our collective future and support the vulnerable amongst us.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: In this way, we can strengthen our social compact and grow our economy at the same time.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: The two objectives will reinforce and support each other, allowing us to move forward while staying together.

sections.label: President's recommendation for financial Bills
sections.summary: Article 59(2) requires the President's recommendation, given on Government advice, for Bills with financial implications.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: Mr Chairman, under Article 59(2) of the Constitution, Bills or amendments with financial implications cannot be introduced or moved in this House without the President’s recommendation.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: This mechanism ensures that the Government of the day has the sole right and responsibility to initiate financial legislation and therefore financial legislation cannot proceed without the Government’s support.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: It is very important to understand in this context, that for the purposes of Article 59(2), when the President gives his or her recommendation, it is upon the advice of the Government and not at the discretion of the President.

sections.label: Minister's duties for Government Bills
sections.summary: A Minister must indicate whether the President's recommendation is required and signify if it was obtained.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: For a Government Bill falling within the scope of Article 59(2), the Minister giving notice of the introduction of the Bill must indicate whether the President's recommendation is required and when introducing the Bill at First Reading, must signify whether the recommendation has been obtained.

sections.label: Cabinet Minister signifies recommendation
sections.summary: A Cabinet Minister must signify whether the President's recommendation was obtained before a leave Motion is moved.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: If the Minister for Finance informs the Speaker that the President's recommendation is in fact required, then, before the Member can be called upon to move the Motion seeking leave to introduce this Bill under Standing Order 66(1), a Cabinet Minister must signify to Parliament whether the President's recommendation has been obtained.

sections.label: Urgency and Contingency Fund reasons
sections.summary: The reasons were market sensitivity and an opportune time to develop Kallang Alive precinct; the termination sum is paid this financial year.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: The reasons for the urgency and the use of the Contingency Fund was: first, the transaction was market sensitive; and second, it was an opportune time to develop the Kallang Alive precinct as the sports sector recovered from COVID-19.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: The termination sum will be paid in this financial year.

sections.label: Audit of $72.3 billion
sections.summary: The audit of the full $72.3 billion will be completed by the end of FY2024.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: For his fourth question, the audit of the full $72.3 billion will be completed by the end of FY2024.

sections.label: Draw on reserves
sections.summary: Taking or drawing down principal, or alienating land not made good, is a draw on the reserves.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: When the principal amount is taken or drawn down or when land is alienated and if it is not made good or put back, that is a draw on the reserves.

sections.label: Government authority and Parliament oversight
sections.summary: The Government is elected to govern and is accountable to Parliament, which scrutinises broad policy rather than day-to-day operations.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: I think his first question is related to what authority does the Government have and what is the relationship with Parliament and the degree of oversight.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: I should start off with the first premise, which is that when the people elect the Government, it is to govern.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: Hence, when the Government is accountable, it has to come back to Parliament for various things.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: But when it comes to Parliament, it is usually to scrutinise broad policy and not the day-to-day operational matters.

sections.label: Parliament scrutiny of budget details
sections.summary: Parliament approves broad expenditure, while spending details fall to Ministries, and can be queried via Parliamentary Questions or the Estimates Committee.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: You approve the financial policy, all those broad headings and the broad expenditure that is agreed to by Parliament, but the details of how that is to be spent if it is within the block budget, that is really within the Ministries' purview.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: But if it is thought, for example, that the Ministry has not done well in its expenditure, that can be queried in Parliament either through Parliamentary Questions, and we also have the Estimates Committee, which is a standing Parliamentary Select Committee which examines the Government's Budget and raises questions thereon.

sections.label: Debating reserves framework changes
sections.summary: Anyone wanting to change the reserves framework can debate it.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: If you want to change the reserves framework, by all means, you can debate that.

sections.label: Pro-Enterprise Panel and Go-Business portal
sections.summary: The Pro-Enterprise Panel solicits business feedback, and Go-Business licensing portal cut food-related licence processing by up to 14 days and reduced forms.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: One of the initiatives, Mr Liang is aware, is the Pro-Enterprise Panel under the Ministry of Trade and Industry (MTI) where we regularly solicit feedback from businesses and from trade associations on where are some of the pain points and where are some of the areas for improvement.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: I recall, a few years ago, when I was with MTI, I shared an example of how we used business process, re-engineering and digital transformation to implement Go-Business licensing portal where we shortened the processing time for food-related businesses when they applied for licenses by up to 14 days and we cut down the number of forms that they need to submit.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: Previously, I think it was 14 altogether, more than 800 data fields.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: We did some consolidation and we reduced it to one form with fewer than 90 data fields, and we removed some of the duplicate licences and helped them to save on licensing fees.

sections.label: President consulting Council of Presidential Advisors
sections.summary: The President must consult the Council of Presidential Advisors before exercising discretionary power, except for excluded matters in Article 37I(A)2.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: Sorry, Mr Chairman, I just wanted to clarify something to make sure I was absolutely accurate in my answer to Mr Leon Perera earlier, about when the President consults the Council of Presidential Advisors (CPA).

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: I just wanted to clarify that the President must consult the Council before exercising any discretionary power, unless it is one of the excluded matters in Article 37I(A)2, that she only needed to consult in some situations.

sections.label: Targeted e-invoice adoption rate
sections.summary: A clarification is sought on the targeted adoption rate for e-invoice for transactions with the Government.

sentences.speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har
sentences.text: The second clarification is, what is the targeted adoption rate for e-invoice for transaction with Government?

sections.label: Government supplier payment term
sections.summary: The Government's current payment term for suppliers is within 30 days.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: Mr Chairman, the current payment term for the Government to pay our suppliers is within 30 days.

sections.label: Aim for 14-day payment
sections.summary: For simpler, more straightforward contracts and smaller amounts, the aim is to pay within 14 days.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: Rather than to have sort of a blanket yes or no, we will certainly aim to work towards where we can – for simpler, more straightforward contracts, smaller amounts, we try our best to go within 14 days.

sections.label: Smaller projects and savings ideas
sections.summary: Smaller projects may not yield much savings alone but could add up, and officers' suggestions and pilots will be supported.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: Mr Chairman, Mr Saktiandi raised an important point because we do not just focus on the large ticket items.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: Those are very important, because, as I mentioned in my speech earlier, we managed to save $1 billion dollars through the process together with experts from private sector and academia.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: But many of the smaller projects on their own, may not yield a lot of savings.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: But if you add them all up and there are many of them, could make a positive impact on our overall value-for -money outcome.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: What we want to do is continue this process of working closely with them, letting our officers know that when you bring up such suggestions, you will be supported.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: We will facilitate experimentation, trying out some of these new ideas.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: And even if some of them were to fail along the way, because we are doing some pilots and it is not guaranteed that all of these would succeed, it is okay.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: It is okay to try because we are all working towards a better outcome.
